subject: Post-demo: 1M token target & comparative $/1M pricing sketch
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia@medminds.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: 1M token target & comparative $/1M pricing sketch

Hi Alicia — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our demo and pricing discussion:

- Target volume: 1M tokens/month as pilot baseline (you gave a mid-range estimate 800k—1.2M).
- Budget band: you indicated $6k–$12k/mo for inference (firm-level budget constraint).
- Primary objectives: reduce latency for interactive features, predictable unit costs, and a fall-back path for degraded SLAs.

Requested from you: confirmation of the preferred billing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly commit) and whether you need SOC2 evidence up front.

Attached I’m sending a quick benchmarking sketch that compares a Redwood Dedicated pilot price vs. common public-host offers (OpenAI, Anthropic) and a few managed open-model hosts. The attachment contains our suggested anchor and two scenarios:

- Scenario A: conservative (cache-heavy, 20% token reduction)
- Scenario B: aggressive (KV caching + batching, 35% token reduction)

Action items:
1) Alicia: confirm budget band + billing cadence by EOD Friday so we can draft an SOW.
2) Ben: prepare a 60-day pilot pricing + SLA note to include dedicated GPU pool estimate.
3) Laura: pull SOC2 + data retention docs and add to the shared folder.

Thanks — attaching the sketch now. If you want, we can run a micro benchmark on a sample payload next week.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_pricing_v1.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: mm_proposal_pricing_grid.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Alicia Ramos <alicia@medminds.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medminds.ai
Date: 2028-11-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: 1M token target & comparative $/1M pricing sketch

Jordan — thanks for the recap and for the attachments. Quick answers: 

- Budget: our controller gave a preliminary band of $7k–$10k/mo for the first 3 months; could expand with proven latency and cost savings.
- Billing: monthly preferred; we can do quarterly commit if there is a significant discount.
- SOC2: yes please — we need the attestation for procurement review.

A couple of clarifying questions on your benchmark:
1) When you list $/1M token numbers, are those post-cache (effective) or gross tokens?
2) Do the OpenAI/Anthropic comparisons reflect streaming vs non-streaming pricing differences?

We’ll review the spreadsheet and aim to get feedback by Monday. Also what does the pilot onboarding timeline look like — can you start infra in ~2 weeks?

Best,
Alicia Ramos
Head of Product
MedMinds
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia@medminds.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-07T12:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: 1M token target & comparative $/1M pricing sketch

Alicia — quick clarifications inline and a short synthesis from the attachment so procurement has clear numbers to evaluate.

Answers:
- The $/1M figures in our sheet show both gross token list price and an "effective $/1M" after expected caching and batching gains. The primary column to share with procurement is the effective $/1M.
- OpenAI/Anthropic rows in the sheet are normalized to streaming-equivalent token billing where applicable; we also add a note where host billing is per-request or per-inference to avoid apples-to-oranges comparisons.

Synthesis (pilot = 1M tokens/month):
- OpenAI (gpt-4.1 style host estimate): gross $/1M = $35; effective after caching (20%) = ~$28.
- Anthropic (claude-like): gross $/1M = $30; effective = ~$24.
- Typical managed open-model hosts (quantized Llama variants): gross $/1M = $12–$18; effective = $9–$15 depending on cache-hit rates and model size.
- Redwood Dedicated pilot (our proposed): gross $/1M = $16 (includes reserved capacity amortization); effective = $11 with conservative caching and batching.

Net takeaways: for MedMinds’ latency and control needs, Redwood Dedicated sits between Anthropic/OpenAI and the cheapest managed open-hosts on gross cost, but provides better predictability and lower tail-latency. If you can commit quarterly, we can push the effective $/1M toward $9–$10 in an aggressive optimization path (quantization + tighter batching).

Pilot onboarding and timing:
- Standard onboard (SOC2 review + infra provisioning) = 10 business days once SOW is signed.
- If you approve a light-weight pilot (no heavy integrations) we can spin up a sandbox cluster in ~5 business days; measurement window 2 weeks.

I’ve attached a one-page summary (redwood_pricing_v1.pdf) and the raw grid (mm_proposal_pricing_grid.xlsx) that shows assumptions per row. Calling out the key variables used to compute effective $/1M: average tokens per request, cache hit rate, KV-cache effectiveness, and sequence length distribution.

Next steps proposed:
- Alicia: confirm monthly vs. quarterly cadence and whether a 60-day pilot is acceptable.
- Ben: draft SOW and pilot pricing sheet for procurement.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call with procurement next week.

Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mm_proposal_pricing_grid.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia@medminds.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-07T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: 1M token target & comparative $/1M pricing sketch

Alicia — looping in procurement next steps and a pragmatic SOW approach. High level pilot offer we can put on the table now: 

- 60-day pilot: $9,500/month (monthly billing), includes up to 1.2M gross tokens per month, 99.8% regional uptime SLA, and one optimization workshop midway.
- Optional quarterly commit: $25,000 for 3 months (saves ~12% vs monthly).
- Add-on: additional SOC2 artifact bundle + onboarding concierge for $2,000 one-time.

We’ll include specific pass/fail acceptance criteria in the SOW (latency P95 under X ms for sample workload, <Y cost drift). Jordan will coordinate test payloads and Laura will share SOC2 docs to the Drive link.

If this aligns with the band Alicia quoted, I’ll draft a simple SOW and share a DocuSign link by EOD Monday.

Thanks — Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
